Search Console is open on **kuchup.com** as `a.mortezaie98@gmail.com`. I pulled the last 3 months and submitted the sitemap — it had never been submitted.

**The 7-vs-6 indexing scare is a red herring.** Almost all organic demand is brand, and several real marketing URLs are still missing from the index.

### Last 3 months
| | |
|---|---|
| Clicks | **20** |
| Impressions | **328** |
| CTR | **6.1%** |
| Avg position | **18.4** |

**13 of those 20 clicks are the query `kuchup`.** Non-brand queries exist (`visa sponsored jobs in netherlands`, `germany software engineer jobs visa sponsorship`, etc.) but they are 1 impression each. Google has seen the intent; it has not decided the site deserves those rankings yet.

### What is actually indexed
Indexed (6): `/`, `/how-it-works`, Germany, Netherlands, Portugal, and **www** Ireland.

Not in the index: **`/relocation-jobs-uk`**, **`/pricing`**, **`/mcp`**, and apex **`/relocation-jobs-ireland`**.

The 7 “not indexed” URLs are noise: www/http redirects, `/panel` (correctly blocked), and an old Next.js `.woff2` font file.

### What I already did
Submitted `https://kuchup.com/sitemap.xml` (9 URLs). Google will process it over the next days.

### Real issues, in order
1. **Homepage `Last-Modified` is 31 Dec 2098.** That date is also in the sitemap. Google treats future dates as junk; this is a server file-mtime bug, not a content problem.
2. **UK / pricing / MCP / apex Ireland are not indexed.** Sitemap submit should help; URL Inspection → Request indexing would speed it up.
3. **Country pages are the only non-brand foothold.** NL 114 impressions / 3 clicks, DE 124 / 2, PT 43 / 0. Those pages need more unique substance than a template, or they will stay around position 18.
4. **`/how-it-works` is 156 impressions / 1 click.** Visibility without a snippet people click.

I would not spend time on the redirect/canonical “errors.” www already 301s to apex.

Want me to start with the **2098 lastmod fix**, **request indexing for the missing 4 URLs**, or **thicken the country landing pages**?

input.plan:
# Kuchup SEO correctness

GSC (3 months, Web, last update ~3.5h ago): **20 clicks / 328 impressions / position 18.4**. **13/20 clicks are branded `kuchup`**. Indexed: `/`, `/how-it-works`, DE, NL, PT, **www Ireland**. Missing: **UK, pricing, MCP, apex Ireland**. Sitemap was empty; it is now submitted.

The 7 “not indexed” URLs are not the problem: 4 www/http redirects (correct), www Portugal duplicate (already 301s), `/panel?country=germany` (correctly blocked), and a leftover `/_next/...woff2`.

Country pages already have visa routes, FAQs, and baked-in catalog snapshots. A blog/cluster program is not the next move. Technical correctness + internal linking + one CTR title fix will move this site more than new copy.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph indexable [Should be indexed]
    Home["/"]
    How["/how-it-works"]
    Price["/pricing"]
    Mcp["/mcp"]
    Countries["/relocation-jobs-*"]
  end
  subgraph private [Must stay out]
    Panel["/panel"]
    NextAssets["/_next assets"]
    Www["www and http"]
  end
  Home --> How
  Home --> Price
  Home --> Mcp
  Home --> Countries
  Www -->|"301"| Home
  Panel -->|"robots Disallow"| private
```

## What we will not do

- Validate-fix GSC redirect/canonical buckets (www already 301s to apex).
- Block `/_next/` in robots.txt (that hides CSS/JS from Googlebot).
- Run the full 15-agent claude-seo crawl (local Python is 3.9; GSC already gave the truth).
- Write a content mill or keyword cluster. Country templates are already substantial.

## Phase 1 — Technical correctness (code)

**1. Never emit a future `lastmod` / `Last-Modified`**

Production homepage sends `Last-Modified: 31 Dec 2098` and sitemap `<lastmod>2098-12-31</lastmod>`. Google ignores or distrusts future dates ([seo-sitemap](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/build-sitemap): lastmod must be a real content change).

Clamp in [`relocation_jobs/web/server.py`](relocation_jobs/web/server.py) `_mtime_lastmod`: if mtime is after UTC today, use today (or omit lastmod). Also set `Last-Modified` on marketing HTML responses from the same clamped value so Flask/`send_from_directory` cannot leak the 2098 file timestamp.

Extend [`tests/web/test_public_api.py`](tests/web/test_public_api.py) `test_public_seo_endpoints_are_available`: every sitemap `<lastmod>` is `<=` today.

**2. Canonical = sitemap loc**

Live homepage canonical is `https://kuchup.com` (no slash); sitemap loc is `https://kuchup.com/`. Pick one: **apex home with trailing slash**, all other marketing URLs without trailing slash.

- Next: [`homepage/app/layout.tsx`](homepage/app/layout.tsx) `alternates.canonical` → `https://kuchup.com/`.
- Flask sitemap already builds `{public_site_url}{path}` with path `/` → that is the slash form. Keep it.

**3. Remove invalid SearchAction**

[`homepage/app/layout.tsx`](homepage/app/layout.tsx) advertises `https://kuchup.com/?q={search_term_string}`. The hero search is a client form with `preventDefault` and **does not read `?q=`**. Google sitelinks searchbox schema that 404s/noops is worse than none. Drop `potentialAction` from the `WebSite` node. Keep Organization + SoftwareApplication.

**4. Stop Google indexing `/_next` binaries**

Keep serving `/_next/<path>` (needed for the static export). On [`homepage_next_assets`](relocation_jobs/web/server.py) add `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` so font/JS URLs cannot reappear as “pages”.

**5. Rebuild static export after homepage metadata changes**

Source of truth is `homepage/` → `npm run build:flask` → [`relocation_jobs/static/homepage/`](relocation_jobs/static/homepage/). Flask only serves the export. Deploy via existing `maybe_build_homepage` in [`scripts/ec2_app_deploy.sh`](scripts/ec2_app_deploy.sh).

FAQPage JSON-LD on country/MCP pages: Google retired FAQ rich results (May 2026). Leave the visible FAQ HTML (GEO citability). Do not spend a pass deleting FAQPage unless we are already in those files.

## Phase 2 — Indexation via links (the real gap)

Header in [`homepage/components/Header.tsx`](homepage/components/Header.tsx) points “How it works” at **`/#how-it-works`** (homepage fragment). Footer correctly uses `/how-it-works`, `/pricing`, `/mcp`. That is why GSC lists hash URLs (`#countries`, `#product`, `#access`) and why **pricing/MCP/UK were easy to miss**.

Change primary nav to indexable routes:

- How it works → `/how-it-works` (keep `id="how-it-works"` on the homepage section for in-page jumps only)
- Add **Pricing** → `/pricing` (currently footer-only; not indexed)
- Keep MCP → `/mcp`
- Countries can stay `/#countries` (that section already links every `/relocation-jobs-*` page)

Country CTAs that go to `/panel?country=` are fine for users; `/panel` stays in `PRIVATE_ROBOTS_DISALLOW`. Do not “SEO-open” the panel. The public catalog on the country page is the indexable proof.

## Phase 3 — One on-page CTR fix

`/how-it-works`: **156 impressions / 1 click**. Title is generic `How It Works | Relocation Jobs`.

Rewrite title + meta in [`homepage/app/how-it-works/page.tsx`](homepage/app/how-it-works/page.tsx) to the actual query class (visa-sponsored software jobs / how the catalog works), e.g. title **How Kuchup finds visa-sponsored software jobs in Europe**. Keep H1 readable. Align Open Graph.

Do not rewrite Germany/NL/PT country copy in this pass. They already match the non-brand queries GSC showed (`visa sponsored jobs in netherlands`, `germany software engineer jobs visa sponsorship`); they need time + the sitemap, not a second template.

## Phase 4 — After deploy (GSC, not more code)

In Search Console (already open as `a.mortezaie98@gmail.com`):

1. Confirm sitemap `https://kuchup.com/sitemap.xml` shows Success and 9 discovered URLs (not 2098 lastmod).
2. URL Inspection → Request indexing: `/relocation-jobs-uk`, `/pricing`, `/mcp`, `/relocation-jobs-ireland`.
3. Ignore redirect/duplicate/robots rows.

Optional later (not this plan): privacy/terms page (E-E-A-T trust), Google API service account for automated GSC pulls, country-page thickening if those URLs stay at position ~18 after they are indexed.

## Verification

- `pytest tests/web/test_public_api.py -o addopts=` (sitemap lastmod clamp + existing SEO endpoints).
- Curl production after deploy: homepage `Last-Modified` not in 2098; sitemap lastmod `<=` today; `/_next` responses include `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`.
- Spot-check exported HTML: homepage canonical `https://kuchup.com/`; no SearchAction; header links to `/how-it-works` and `/pricing`.

Next.js still emits the homepage canonical as `https://kuchup.com` (no slash) even when we set `https://kuchup.com/`. The sitemap loc uses the slash form. Google treats those as the same URL for the root.

You have access to tools through dynamic namespaces, e.g. MCP servers, using `GetDynamicTools` and `CallDynamicTool`.

## Dynamic Tool Discovery and Invocation

Use `GetDynamicTools` to discover tool schemas, then `CallDynamicTool` to invoke one tool. Aim to minimize round-trips: ideally one discovery call followed by one invocation.

If the user mentions a product or service represented by an available namespace, and the request likely depends on it, proactively inspect that namespace before answering. If you are unsure which namespace matches, search with a relevant pattern.

`GetDynamicTools` supports these modes:

1. `{"namespace":"<id>"}`: returns schemas and full descriptions for every tool in that namespace.
2. `{"namespace":"<id>","toolName":"<name>"}`: returns one tool schema with its full description.
3. `{"pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches namespace and tool names.
4. `{"namespace":"<id>","pattern":"<regex>"}`: searches tools within one namespace.
5. No arguments: returns the full catalog.

Pattern-search and catalog results shorten long descriptions, marked by a trailing "... [truncated]"; namespace and single-tool lookups always return the complete description.

Always inspect a tool's schema before invoking it with `CallDynamicTool`.

If the available dynamic tools do not fully support what the user asked you to do, complete the work you can with the current tool set. In your work summary, include what you were unable to do and why. Do not use browser automation to work around missing tools unless the user explicitly asks you to use the browser.

content.text:
Google is not hiding a secret keyword list, and those visa phrases are not “indexed keywords.” Google indexes **URLs**. Queries are just how people search. Kuchup already appears for some of those phrases — too far down the page for anyone to click.

### What the query table actually shows

Last 3 months, Web:

| Named query | Clicks | Impressions |
|---|---|---|
| **kuchup** | **13** | **157** |
| intalento visa relocation platform germany | 0 | 8 |
| visa sponsored jobs in netherlands | 0 | 1 |
| it jobs in portugal with visa sponsorship | 0 | 1 |
| germany software engineer jobs visa sponsorship | 0 | 1 |
| german work visa for programmers | 0 | 1 |
| visa for tech specialists germany | 0 | 1 |
| **Named total** | **13** | **170** |
| **Site total** | **20** | **328** |

The other **7 clicks and ~158 impressions** are real. Google **does not name** queries that are too rare (privacy). Insights for the last 28 days only lists **`kuchup` (70% of clicks)**. That is the “just Kuchup” effect: the table is brand-only because everything else is either 1 impression at position ~18, or anonymized.

Those visa queries **are** matching your country pages. They are not ranking. Average position for the site is **18.4** — page 2. Page 2 impressions without clicks is normal; it is not a redirect.

### Other panels (same 3 months)

**Insights (28 days):** 7 clicks, 163 impressions. Pages that got clicks: homepage (5), Germany (1), Netherlands (1). Query that got clicks: only `kuchup`.

**Countries:** clicks are not from the job markets. Armenia 6, India 5, Pakistan 3, Germany 2. The US has 46 impressions and 0 clicks.

**Devices:** desktop 13 / 177, mobile 7 / 148.

**Search appearance:** no data — only normal blue links. No sitelinks, FAQ, or other rich results.

**Links:** **1 external backlink**, from `github.com`, anchor `https kuchup com`. That is why competitive queries cannot rank. Google has almost no independent sites saying “this is the visa-jobs tool.”

The www / `#access` / `#product` rows are **URL variants**, not extra keywords. www already 301s to the apex; Google still counted old www Ireland/Germany impressions.

### What this means

You cannot “index a keyword.” You index a page, then Google may show it for many queries. Today:

- Brand search (`kuchup`) works.
- Intent search (visa + country + software) already sees the site, around position 18, with 0 clicks.
- The missing named queries in the table are mostly **anonymized low-volume searches**, plus those 6 visa phrases you did not write titles for but Google still associated with the country pages.

Indexing UK / pricing / MCP (which we requested) adds **pages**. It will not make `visa sponsored jobs in netherlands` jump from position 18 to page 1 by itself. That needs time, more unique country-page substance, and links from somewhere other than GitHub.

If you want a next move, the highest leverage is **country-page titles/H1s that match those 6 named queries**, not more GSC request-indexing.

content.text:
Live now. Each country page had the same title pattern (`Visa Sponsorship for Software Jobs in {country}`), so Google had nothing specific to rank for those queries. They now use the phrases people actually searched.

| Page | Title / H1 now matches |
|---|---|
| [Germany](https://kuchup.com/relocation-jobs-germany) | `germany software engineer jobs visa sponsorship` plus FAQ/H2 for `german work visa for programmers` and `visa for tech specialists germany` |
| [Netherlands](https://kuchup.com/relocation-jobs-netherlands) | `visa sponsored jobs in netherlands` |
| [Portugal](https://kuchup.com/relocation-jobs-portugal) | `it jobs in portugal with visa sponsorship` |
| UK / Ireland | Same shape, so they are not clones of Germany |

I did **not** put **Intalento** in the Germany title. That query is someone looking for a competitor. Stuffing their brand into our tags is spam; Google already associated Kuchup with that search as a related result.

Compare-country links now use those titles as anchor text, so the pages also point at each other with the same language.

This does not make those queries jump to page 1 this week. It gives Google a clean title/H1 to recrawl against instead of a generic template. Rankings still sit around position 18 until there is more than one GitHub backlink.

content.text:
Google already found Kuchup. Best-practice SEO from here is not more keywords. It is **be the most useful result for those visa-job queries, then get other sites to point at you**.

That is Google’s own bar: [people-first content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) (Who / How / Why) plus [how Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) (discover via links and sitemaps, rank by relevance + quality + PageRank). Helpful content is no longer a separate “update”; it is part of core ranking.

### Where you actually are

| Layer | Status |
|---|---|
| Technical | Fine enough: HTTPS, sitemap, canonicals, titles live |
| Relevance | Country pages already get **impressions** at ~position 18 |
| Competitiveness | **1 backlink** (GitHub). Brand clicks from AM/IN/PK, not DE/NL seekers |
| SERP type | Those queries rank **guides** (Euro Top Tech, Next Level Jobs, VisaMatch), not generic homepages |

Titles were the right first fix. They tell Google what the page is. They do not beat a 2026 guide that lists “18 companies that sponsor in Germany” unless your page is **more useful than that guide**.

Google’s test you currently fail: *“Does this provide original information vs other pages in the results?”* and *“Would someone bookmark this?”* Kuchup’s original asset is the **career-page catalog**. The visa copy is similar to every other explainer. Catalog snapshots dated **22 Aug 2026** look stale next to “2026 Blue Card threshold” blogs.

Visa/immigration is close to YMYL (money/legal). Trust matters more here than on a normal SaaS landing page. There is still no clear **who wrote this** or **how the catalog is built**.

### What “up” means, in order

**1. Make each country page the best answer (this week–month)**  
Keep one URL per country. Do not start a blog mill. Google explicitly warns against publishing lots of topics hoping some rank.

On Germany / NL / PT the page should do what the ranking blogs do, plus what they cannot:

- A dated, first-party block: “As of {date}, Kuchup sees **N companies** and **M visa-positive software roles** on employer career pages.” That is Experience, not rewritten visa law.
- A short **How we know**: 6-hour scrape of career pages, not aggregator listings; visa flag method in one paragraph; official gov links already on the page.
- A **Who**: About / byline. “Relocation Jobs / Kuchup, built by …” with a real person. Anonymous visa advice loses YMYL trust.
- Keep UK, `/pricing`, `/mcp` indexed so the site is not a handful of orphans.

Falsifiable: GSC average position for those named queries moves from ~18 toward page 1, and CTR is no longer 0. If titles recrawl and position stays ~18, the page is still weaker than Euro Top Tech, not “unindexed.”

**2. Earn links (this is the ceiling)**  
Google still uses link analysis / PageRank. Sitemap gets you crawled; **other sites** get you trusted. One GitHub link cannot beat established relocation blogs.

People-first ways that match Google’s starter guide (“promote your site,” don’t buy links):

- Post the Germany/NL numbers where engineers already look (HN, r/cscareerquestionsEU, Blind, LinkedIn) with the country URL, not the homepage.
- Ask 5–10 people who already write about EU relocation to cite the catalog as a data source.
- A honest **Kuchup vs Intalento** page is valid for that one GSC query. Putting “Intalento” in the Germany title is not.

**3. Do not do this**  
Mass AI country/blog posts, fake freshness dates, word-count padding, PBNs, stuffing competitor names. Those are what core ranking is built to demote.

### Realistic outcome

| Horizon | Honest target |
|---|---|
| 2–6 weeks | Recrawl of new titles; maybe a few extra named queries in GSC |
| 2–4 months | Non-zero clicks on NL/DE/PT **if** catalog data is unique and a few real links exist |
| 6–12 months | Competitive for head terms only if the site is cited as a source, not just self-branded |

A SaaS template would also add `/compare`, case studies, a blog. For Kuchup that is later. Five strong country pages plus About/method plus links will outrank a 40-post blog with no data.

---

The next implementation that matches this research is: **live dated catalog proof + How we know + About/byline on the country pages** — not more title tweaks.

If you want that, say so and I will do that slice. If you would rather start with the Intalento comparison page or a link-outreach list, say which.
